description: Given a Prefect @task that runs a SQL data-quality assertion — a null-count check, a min-row-count threshold, or a soft logger.warning failure — author the matching Orchestra *_RUN_TEST task with correctly inverted pass/fail semantics: Prefect passes when the assertion is TRUE, Orchestra fails when the threshold expression IS MET.

evals.prompt: Convert this Prefect flow to Orchestra (see files/null_check_order_ids.py). check_no_null_order_ids asserts the null count is exactly zero. Write the pipeline YAML to pipeline.yml in the current directory — no live queries, no deploy.
evals.expected_output: An Orchestra v1 pipeline YAML with a load task for the orders insert, followed by a sequenced SNOWFLAKE_RUN_TEST task for check_no_null_order_ids whose error_threshold_expression is '> 0' — the inverted form of Prefect's assert nulls == 0 — not '= 0'.

assertions.text: Pipeline declares version v1
A SNOWFLAKE_RUN_TEST task is present
At least two task groups are present (load + quality)
Task groups are chained via depends_on (quality runs after load)
The check queries for IS NULL
error_threshold_expression is the inverted '> 0' form (fails when the null count is greater than zero)

The threshold is genuinely inverted from Prefect's assert nulls == 0 — it is '> 0', not a same-direction '= 0' that would (wrongly) fail only when the null count is exactly zero, the opposite of the intended check

Prefect's assert-true-means-pass semantics are correctly flipped: the SQL counts violating (null) rows, and the Orchestra task is written to fail precisely when that count is nonzero, matching what made the original assertion fail

evals.prompt: Convert this Prefect flow to Orchestra (see files/min_row_count_check.py). check_daily_event_volume raises a ValueError if the row count is below 5000. Write the pipeline YAML to pipeline.yml in the current directory — no live queries, no deploy.
evals.expected_output: An Orchestra v1 pipeline YAML with a GCP_BQ_RUN_TEST task for check_daily_event_volume whose error_threshold_expression is '< 5000' — the same-direction threshold matching Prefect's if count < 5000: raise — sequenced after the load task.

assertions.text: Pipeline declares version v1
A GCP_BQ_RUN_TEST task is present
At least two task groups are present (load + quality)
Task groups are chained via depends_on (quality runs after load)
error_threshold_expression fails when the row count is below 5000
The SQL statement returns a single numeric value (a row count), not a raw multi-column or multi-row select

The raise condition's comparator direction is preserved without an extra, unnecessary flip — 'if count < 5000: raise' already fails on the low-count case, so it is not accidentally re-inverted into '>= 5000' or '> 5000'

evals.prompt: Convert this Prefect flow to Orchestra (see files/soft_failure_stale_customers.py). check_customers_freshness only logs a warning when the table is more than 24 hours stale — it never raises, so the flow always continues regardless of the outcome. Write the pipeline YAML to pipeline.yml in the current directory — no live queries, no deploy.
evals.expected_output: An Orchestra v1 pipeline YAML with a POSTGRES_RUN_TEST task for check_customers_freshness carrying warn_threshold_expression: '> 24' and treat_failure_as_warning: true (no hard error_threshold_expression), sequenced after sync_customers, so the pipeline continues with WARNING status instead of failing.

assertions.text: Pipeline declares version v1
A POSTGRES_RUN_TEST task is present
Task groups are chained via depends_on (the freshness check runs after sync_customers)
treat_failure_as_warning is set so the soft check never hard-fails the pipeline
At least one task has treat_failure_as_warning set to true
warn_threshold_expression fires when the table is more than 24 hours stale

No hard error_threshold_expression is set alongside the warning — this check is only ever a WARNING outcome, mirroring logger.warning's non-raising behavior in the Prefect source, not a hard failure with treat_failure_as_warning bolted on top
The SQL still resolves to a single numeric value (hours since the table was last updated) suitable for parameters.statement on a *_RUN_TEST task
